post.description:
Create a payout in one of two ways:
- **Payout without quote** — specify the beneficiary, currencies and amount inline. Fees and the FX
  rate are determined at creation time (`CreatePayoutWithoutQuoteRequest`).

- **Payout with quote** — pass a `quote_id` from `POST /quotes` (with `resource: payout`) to settle
  against a locked rate and fee breakdown. The currencies, amount and payment rail are derived from
  the quote and must not be sent (`CreatePayoutWithQuoteRequest`).

The request variant is selected by the presence of `quote_id`.
If payout queueing is enabled on your account, every payout is accepted with `status: queued`, including one that the balance in the source currency already covers, and a payout the balance does not cover is accepted instead of rejected. Glomo releases it automatically once the balance covers the amount plus fees. Fees and the FX rate are fixed at creation and honoured when the payout is released. Without payout queueing, a short balance is rejected at creation.

400.description:
Bad Request — validation error. For quote-based payouts, possible messages include `quote_id not found`, `quote_id has expired`, `quote_id has already been used`, `source_amount cannot be specified when quote_id is present` (likewise for any other quote-derived field), `Quote is not compatible with the selected beneficiary` (the quote's rail is not supported by the chosen beneficiary), and `Quote is not a payout quote` (the `quote_id` belongs to a payin quote).
When the balance does not cover the payout and payout queueing is not enabled on your account, the message reads `Account has insufficient balance to process this transaction. Additional amount required: N.` where `N` is the shortfall, in the smallest unit of the source currency.

get.description:
Returns a list of your payments, sorted by creation date with the most recent first.

Filters combine with AND, with one exception: `payin_id` and `subscription_id` are mutually exclusive
and sending both returns `400`.

The `status` filter accepts only `in_progress`, `success`, `failed` and `action_required`; any other
value returns `400`. That is not the same set of values a payment can come back with, and the filter
does not map onto the response field one-for-one: a payment returned with `status: under_review` is
matched by `status=in_progress`, and some payments returned with `status: in_progress` are not matched
by `status=in_progress` at all. Treat the filter as a coarse narrowing and read `status` on each
payment you get back.

`compliance_status` is a separate field with its own filter and moves independently of `status`. Most
payments have no compliance status at all, so filtering on it will exclude them.

post.description:
Create an order for checkout in one of two ways:
- **Order without quote** — specify the amount, currency and payment methods inline
  (`Orders`).

- **Order with quote** — pass a `quote_id` from `POST /quotes` (with `resource: payin`) to bind

  `price_id`, `payment_methods`, `split_ids`) must not be sent (`CreateOrderWithQuoteRequest`).
  **When a `quote_id` is supplied, the order's expiry is set to the quote's expiry.**

Pass `split_ids` to declare your share of a dynamic pricing rule's fee for this order. See [Dynamic Fee Split](#tag/pricing_split). If a split on the order later stops resolving — Glomo deleted the underlying rule, or the rule is no longer dynamic — opening the checkout returns a `400 Bad Request`, the order is expired, and you must issue a new one.
To check complete list of API validations, click [here](/platform/validations#validations-for-creating-orders).

Create a shareable URL for a hosted payment page in one of two ways:
- **Payment link without quote** — specify the amount, currency, expiry and payment methods
  inline (`PaymentLink`).

- **Payment link with quote** — pass a `quote_id` from `POST /quotes` (with `resource: payin`) to

Uploads a file and returns a document record you can reference from other resources — as the invoice
or supporting paperwork on a payin or payout, or as evidence when responding to a request for
information (RFI).

Send the request as `multipart/form-data`. The file must be a JPEG, PNG or PDF of at most 10 MB
(10,485,760 bytes), and the uploaded filename and `document_name` at most 128 characters each.

Upload is a separate step from attaching, and each consumer names the reference differently: pass the
returned `id` as `document_id` when creating a payin, an order or a refund, and inside the `documents`
array when creating a payout or responding to an RFI. Check the schema of the endpoint you are
attaching to — the key inside `documents` is not the same on every one. A document that is never
referenced stays listed but has no effect.

post.description:
Creates a price governing the referral fee applied to payins, which you then attach to a payin or an
order by passing its ID as `price_id`. The fee it produces is returned as `referral_fee` on the
payment and in a quote's `fees` breakdown.

Every price created here governs the referral fee — there is no fee type to choose, which is why the
Price object carries no `fee_type` field. `GET /prices` lists these and only these.

`pricing_type` selects the shape of the rule and which other fields are permitted — sending a field
belonging to the other shape is rejected rather than ignored:

- `fixed` requires `fees_amount` and `fees_currency`, and must not include `bps`.

- `percentage` requires `bps`, and must not include `fees_amount` or `fees_currency`.

The first referral-fee price you create becomes your default automatically, whether or not you send
`set_as_default`. After that, sending `set_as_default: true` promotes this price and demotes the
previous default — a business has at most one default referral-fee price at a time. The default is
what applies when a payin does not name a `price_id`.

CreatePayoutWithoutQuoteRequest.title: CreatePayoutWithoutQuoteRequest
CreatePayoutWithoutQuoteRequest.description: Create a payout without a quote by specifying the beneficiary, currencies and amount. Fees and the FX rate are determined at creation time. Use this variant when you have not pre-generated a quote. To create a payout against a locked quote instead, see `CreatePayoutWithQuoteRequest`.

purpose_code.description:
Why you are sending this payout, as a code from a fixed set: see [Payout purpose codes](/payout/purpose-codes). This is not free text. Pass a listed code exactly, for example `S0802`; matching is exact and case-sensitive. Payouts and payins use different sets, so a payin code such as `P1401` is rejected here. An unrecognised code is rejected with `400 Bad Request`.

INR payouts on a local rail (`neft`, `imps`, `rtgs`, `upi`) accept only a subset of the payout codes. A code outside that subset is rejected with `400 Bad Request`, with a message saying the code is not valid for the selected payment rail.

beneficiary_id.description: The unique identifier for the beneficiary.

source_currency.description: The currency of the balance the payout is paid from, as an [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) code from the list above. Any other value returns `400` with a message containing `Source currency is not supported`.

destination_currency.description: The currency in which the beneficiary receives the payout. The currency code is in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format.

source_amount.description:
The amount you intend to send, in the smallest unit of `source_currency` (cents for USD). `100000` is $1,000.00 when `source_currency` is USD.
Exactly one of `source_amount` or `destination_amount` must be provided (not both).

destination_amount.description:
The amount the beneficiary will receive, in the smallest unit of `destination_currency` (paise for INR, cents for USD). `8235000` is ₹82,350.00 when `destination_currency` is INR.
Exactly one of `source_amount` or `destination_amount` must be provided (not both).

payment_rail.description: The payment rail to use for this payout. Each local rail serves one corridor and is only available when `destination_currency` matches it: `upi`, `imps`, `neft`, `rtgs` for `INR`; `ipp`, `fts` for `AED`; `sepa` for `EUR`; `fps` for `GBP`; `npp` for `AUD`. `swift` is used for international transfers and is available on any corridor. The rail must be eligible for the beneficiary and the amount must fall inside the rail's limits. Defaults to `swift` if omitted; a local rail is not selected automatically.

invoice_number.description: An optional invoice reference for this payout, up to 50 characters. It is returned on the payout as `invoice_number`. A longer value returns `400` with a message containing `Invoice number must be 50 characters or less`.

request_id.description: Your unique identifier for this payout, at most 64 characters, used to reject duplicates. If a payout with the same `request_id` already exists on your account, the request is rejected with `409 Conflict` and the message `Record already exists`; no second payout is created and the existing payout is not returned. Look it up with `GET /v1/payouts?request_id=<your_request_id>`. A value longer than 64 characters is rejected with `400`.

If a payout with the same `request_id` already exists on your account, the request is rejected with `409 Conflict` and the message `Record already exists`; no second payout is created and the existing payout is not returned. Look it up with `GET /v1/payouts?request_id=<your_request_id>`. A value longer than 64 characters is rejected with `400`. Resending with the same `quote_id` fails first with `400`, because the quote has already been used; the `409` applies when a new quote is sent with a repeated `request_id`.

status.description:
The status of the payout.

- `pending_approval` — the payout is waiting for a reviewer on your account to approve it. Only
  used when payout approval is turned on for your account.
- `queued` — the payout is waiting for enough balance to cover it. It moves on once funds arrive, or
  fails with `QUEUE_EXPIRED` if they do not arrive in time.
- `in_progress` — the payout has been accepted and is being processed or reviewed.
- `action_required` — glomo needs more information before the payout can proceed. Respond to the
  open RFI to continue.
- `success` — the beneficiary has been paid. Terminal.
- `failed` — the payout could not be completed; see `error_code`. Terminal.
- `cancelled` — the payout was stopped before it was paid. Terminal.

error_code.description:
A machine-readable code describing why the payout failed or was cancelled. `null` unless the
payout is in an error state. The accompanying `error_description` carries the human-readable text.

| Code | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `QUOTE_EXPIRED` | Quote has expired. Please create a new payout with a valid quote. |
| `QUEUE_EXPIRED` | Payout stayed queued for 30 days because the balance did not cover it. No funds were held. |
| `PAYOUT_REJECTED` | Payout was rejected by the bank. Please reach out to support. (default fallback) |
| `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` | The balance no longer covered the payout when it came out of review. No funds were held. |
| `INVALID_BENE_ACCOUNT_NUMBER` | Beneficiary account number is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_ACCOUNT_TYPE` | Beneficiary account type is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_IFSC` | Beneficiary IFSC code is invalid. |
| `INVALID_VPA` | VPA/UPI address is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_NAME` | Beneficiary name is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_ADDRESS` | Beneficiary address or PIN/ZIP code is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_EMAIL` | Beneficiary email is invalid. |
| `INVALID_BENE_CONTACT` | Beneficiary contact/mobile number is invalid. |
| `NAME_MISMATCH` | Remitter and beneficiary names do not match for the selected purpose. |

The type of the payin. This is set only for payments associated to a payin.

status.description:
The status of the payment.

- `in_progress` — the payment has started and has not completed yet.
- `action_required` — glomo needs more information before the payment can complete. Respond to the
  open RFI to continue.
- `under_review` — the information you submitted is being reviewed.
- `success` — the payment completed. Terminal. Funds can still be held for compliance review; see

compliance_status.description:
The compliance review status of the payment. Present only for payments that have been screened for
sanctions or transaction-monitoring holds; `null` for payments that were not screened. This is
separate from `status` — a payment can be `status: success` while `compliance_status` is
`action_required`, meaning the payment itself completed but funds are held pending compliance
review. See the `rfi` field for what's required when `action_required`.

- `under_review` — the payment is being reviewed and its funds are held.
- `action_required` — documents are needed before the review can finish. Respond to the open RFI.
- `approved` — the review passed and the funds are released.
- `rejected` — the payment did not pass the review.

billing_cycles.description:
Total number of billing cycles for the subscription. Required for regular subscriptions, must not be provided for 'as_presented' subscriptions.
A subscription can have a lifetime of 30 years.
Maximum billing cycles therefore depend on interval:
- Monthly (interval_type='month', interval_count=1): max 360 cycles
- Quarterly (interval_type='month', interval_count=3): max 120 cycles
- Half-yearly (interval_type='month', interval_count=6): max 60 cycles
- Yearly (interval_type='year', interval_count=1): max 30 cycles

Send an integer of at least `2` as a JSON number; a string such as `"12"` is rejected. A value below
`2` or above the interval's maximum returns `400`.

Maximum allowed amount per payment for `as_presented` subscriptions, in the smallest unit of `currency` (cents for USD). `5000` is $50.00 when `currency` is USD. A positive integer. Required when `interval_type` is `as_presented`, and must not be provided for regular subscriptions.
Subsequent payments on the subscription cannot exceed this amount.

Start date of the subscription in UTC timezone and ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be today or in the future.
Required for regular subscriptions, must not be provided for 'as_presented' subscriptions.

expires_at.description: Expiration date for the subscription payment link in UTC timezone and ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be today (UTC) or later, and at most 1 calendar month after today (UTC). An earlier date returns `400` with the message `Validation failed: Expires at must be today or in the future`, and a later one returns `400` with `Validation failed: Expires at cannot be more than 1 months from today`. Supported only when `interval_type` is `as_presented`. Sending `split_ids` on a fixed-frequency subscription returns a `400 Bad Request`, because a fixed-frequency plan auto debits without you and so has no point at which to pass a split or replace one that goes stale.

The declaration applies to the first payment, and to every subsequent auto debit that does not pass `split_ids` of its own. See [Create a payment](#tag/Payment) for the auto debit override.

- `paused` — you paused the subscription. Resume it to continue charging.
- `halted` — charging stopped automatically; `halt_reason` says why. It returns to `active` after
  its next successful payment, for example once the customer updates the card. The resume endpoint
  applies only to `paused` subscriptions.
- `action_required` — glomo needs more information before the subscription can proceed. Respond to
  the open RFI to continue.
- `under_review` — the information you submitted is being reviewed. The subscription becomes
  `active` if the review passes and `failed` if it does not.
- `completed` — every billing cycle has been charged. Terminal.

bank_code.description: Code of the customer's bank. Must be a `bank_code` returned by `GET /lrs/banks` for your account, matched exactly and case-sensitively. An LRS order that uses this account must use a quote created for the same `bank_code`, or the order is rejected.

account_number.description: The customer's account number at that bank. Digits only, with a length inside the range that bank accepts. Returned in full, as sent, in the response.

bank_customer_id.description: Optional. The customer's identifier at their bank. For banks that use one, it must contain only digits, with a length inside the range that bank accepts; an invalid value is rejected with `400`.

resource.description:
What the quote prices.

- `payin` — an LRS remittance from a resident Indian customer. Requires `bank_code`.
- `payout` — a withdrawal back to the customer in India. Only `USD` to `INR` is supported, and
  `bank_code` must not be sent.

bank_code.description: Code of the customer's bank, as returned by `GET /lrs/banks`. Required when `resource` is `payin`, and the bank must be enabled for your account. Rejected when `resource` is `payout`.

source_amount.description: The amount to convert, in the smallest unit of `source_currency` (paisa for INR, cents for USD). `4400000` is ₹44,000.00 when `source_currency` is `INR`. Must be a whole number; a string of digits such as `"4400000"` is also accepted. Send a positive integer; an optional leading sign is accepted. A decimal or an exponent is rejected with `400`. On a payin quote, the amount must fall within the minimum and maximum set for the bank, otherwise the request is rejected with `400` and the message states the limit.

source_currency.description: The currency of `source_amount`. Must differ from `target_currency`.

target_currency.description: The currency to convert into. Must differ from `source_currency`.

LrsQuote.description: An LRS quote: the conversion, tax and exchange rate for an LRS remittance or withdrawal.

id.description: Unique identifier of the quote. Pass it as `lrs.lrs_quote_id` on an LRS order.

from.description: The amount the quote converts from: your `source_amount` and `source_currency`.

amount.description: Amount in the smallest unit of `currency` (paisa for INR, cents for USD).

to.description:
The amount the quote converts to, in `target_currency`.

- `INR` to `USD` payin quote: GST is deducted from `from.amount` before conversion, so
  `to.amount` is the USD remitted.
- `USD` to `INR` payin quote: `to.amount` is the INR equivalent of `from.amount`, plus any
  transaction fee charged to the customer, with GST added.
- Payout quote: `to.amount` is the INR the customer receives after fees and GST are deducted.

On a payin quote, the side in `USD` is the amount an LRS order must be created for.

amount.description: Amount in the smallest unit of `currency` (paisa for INR, cents for USD). `51763` is $517.63 when `currency` is `USD`.

fx_rate.description: The exchange rate applied to the quote, as a decimal string in INR per 1 USD. It is expressed this way whichever direction the quote converts.

bank_code.description: The `bank_code` the quote was created for. Present on payin quotes only.

total_tax.description: GST on the conversion, in paisa, whichever direction the quote converts. `7906` is ₹79.06.

expires_at.description: When the quote expires, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. Payout quotes expire 30 minutes after `created_at`. For payin quotes, rely on this value rather than a fixed duration. An LRS order created from the quote expires at the same time, and an order cannot be created from an expired quote.

created_at.description: When the quote was created, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC.

Notes.description: Optional key-value pairs for attaching custom metadata (e.g. invoice references, project codes). Keys must be strings and cannot collide with reserved field names. If your business has custom field rules configured (e.g. enum constraints), values are validated against those rules. Each key appears as a separate column in CSV report exports, with corresponding values populating the rows.

id.description: The unique identifier for the Document.

rfi_doc_id.description: The unique identifier for the RFI Document. This will be `null` if the document is not an RFI Document.

amount.description: A positive integer representing the smallest currency unit.  For example, if the amount is $299.00, then pass 29900 in this field.  In the case of three decimal currencies, such as KWD, BHD and OMR, to represent an amount of 295.991, pass the value as 295990.  And in the case of zero decimal currencies such as JPY, for amount ￥295, pass the value as 295.

currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, USD.

amount.description: The fee amount in the smallest unit of this entry's `currency` (cents for USD), aggregated across all rules for this fee bearer. `250` is $2.50 when `currency` is USD.

currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, USD.

collection_mode.description: When the fee is collected. Customer-borne fees are always collected immediately; merchant-borne fees follow the payment's collection mode.

taxes.description: Taxes applied on this fee (for example, GST). Empty when no tax applies to the underlying rules.

SplitIds.description:
The pricing splits to apply, each entry an `id` returned by [Create a pricing split](#tag/pricing_split). A split fixes your share of a dynamic rule's fee and the customer bears the remainder. Omit `split_ids` and no dynamic rule is applied — pricing falls back to your normal (non-dynamic) rules.

`split_ids` and `payment_methods` are independent. `payment_methods` restricts which methods the checkout offers. `split_ids` only changes how the fee for a method is priced: a split applies to its own payment method whether or not that method appears in `payment_methods`, and a split never adds a method to the checkout or removes one from it. One checkout can therefore price one method from a dynamic split and another method from your normal rules.

Every id must exist, must belong to your business, and must still point at a live dynamic rule. When two dynamic rules share a dimension — the same payment method, subtype, rail, currency and fee type — declare a split for every one of them or the request is rejected. On payment links and orders, a split whose payment method is not enabled for your business is also rejected.

A subscription only ever charges `card`, or `pay_via_bank` when SEPA-eligible, so a split declared for any other payment method is rejected at subscription creation and on an auto debit. An auto-debit override must be declared for the method the subscription actually charges.

Glomo can configure your account to require a declaration. On such an account, a payment link, an order, a payin quote or an `as_presented` subscription that omits `split_ids` is rejected.

Product.description: Details of the product that the payment is related to.

example.name: REDACTED
example.description: Flexible insurance for belongings travel and digital assets easy to manage

LrsOrderDetails.description:
Send this object to create an LRS order: a remittance from a customer resident in India, funded
from their Indian bank account. If you send `lrs`, `lrs_quote_id` and `remittance_information` are
required.

- Create the quote first with `POST /lrs/quotes`. The order's `amount` must equal the `USD` side of
  the quote (`from.amount` for a `USD` source quote, `to.amount` for an `INR` source quote), and
  `currency` must be `USD`. Otherwise the order is rejected with `400`.
- The quote must not have expired. The order expires when the quote does.
- The customer's country must be India, otherwise the order is rejected with `400`.
- An LRS order doesn't store `invoice_number`, `invoice_description`, `invoice_amount`,
  `reference_number`, `document_id` or `product`; they come back as `null` or are left out. A value
  you send is still validated, so leave these fields out.

Returned on the order when it was created as an LRS order.

lrs_quote_id.description: The `id` of a quote from `POST /lrs/quotes`, created by your account.

remittance_information.description: Your reference for the remittance. Up to 20 characters, using only letters, digits and hyphens; spaces and other characters are rejected with `400`.

bank_account_id.description: The `id` of the customer's LRS bank account, from `POST /customer/{id}/bank_account`. Optional. It must belong to this customer and be at the same bank as the quote's `bank_code`. A bank account from `POST /customer/{id}/bank-accounts` is not accepted here.

beneficiary_id.description: The `id` of a beneficiary created with `category: lrs` through `POST /v2/beneficiaries`, to receive the remittance. Optional.

Amount.description: The amount in the smallest currency unit. For example, if the amount is $299.00, then 29900 is passed in  this field. In the case of three decimal currencies, such as KWD, BHD and OMR, to represent an amount of 295.991, pass the value as 295990. And in the case of zero decimal currencies such as JPY, for amount ￥295, pass the value as 295.

IntervalType.description: Used in combination with interval_count to define the billing cycle frequency.

IntervalCount.description:
Number of intervals between a billing cycle, used in combination with interval_type.
Valid combinations:
- Monthly: interval_type='month', interval_count=1
- Quarterly: interval_type='month', interval_count=3
- Half-yearly: interval_type='month', interval_count=6
- Yearly: interval_type='year', interval_count=1
- As Presented: interval_type='as_presented', interval_count=null

amount.description: The tax amount in the smallest unit of this line's `currency` (cents for USD). `1800` is $18.00 when `currency` is USD.

currency.description: The currency code in [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) format. For example, USD.

name.description: The name of the tax applied on the fee. For example, GST.

bps.description: The tax rate in basis points. For example, 1800 represents 18%.

BeforeParam.name: before
BeforeParam.description: Return only resources created at or before this time. Send an [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) timestamp with an offset, such as `2025-02-18T12:03:44Z` or `2025-02-18T17:33:44+05:30`. A timestamp without an offset is read as UTC. A bare date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) means the end of that day in UTC (`23:59:59.999999Z`). An invalid value returns `400 Bad Request`. Use this to avoid page drift. See [Pagination parameters](/platform/pagination#parameters) for more details.

AfterParam.name: after
AfterParam.description: Return only resources created at or after this time. Send an [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) timestamp with an offset, such as `2025-01-18T12:03:44Z` or `2025-01-18T17:33:44+05:30`. A timestamp without an offset is read as UTC. A bare date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) means the start of that day in UTC (`00:00:00Z`). An invalid value returns `400 Bad Request`. Use this to avoid page drift. See [Pagination parameters](/platform/pagination#parameters) for more details.

PerPageParam.name: per_page
PerPageParam.description: Number of resources per page. Should be between 1 and 100.

PageParam.name: page
PageParam.description: Page number for pagination. Starts from 1. Get the next page number from the `next` field in the response.
